newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's Bourgas shipyard ends strike.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's Bourgas shipyard ends strike.

text.p: Bulgaria's shipyard in the Black Sea port of Bourgas ended a one-day strike on Tuesday after workers received guarantees that their demands for higher wages and replacement of the current management would be met.

"We decided to resume work after industry ministry officials assured us that everything possible would be done to fulfil our demands," the shipyard's trade union leader Velichko Evtimov told Reuters by telephone from Bourgas.

More than half of the 1,200 workers in the Bourgas shipyard, 450 km (280 miles) east of Sofia, went on strike on Monday demanding a 150 percent wage increase, which their director Todor Georgiev said was unrealistic and would violate the goverment's cost cutting policy.
A meeting with the industry ministry, supervising the shipyard, was scheduled for Wednesday, where the shipyard's trade unions expect to negotiate, said Evtimov.
The workers also demanded replacement of current management accusing it of failing to provide sufficient work load and not showing a 1997 work plan.
Industry ministry officials were not available for comment.

In a bid to curb budget spending as part of introducing an IMF-prescribed currency board system in July, Bulgaria's cabinet issued a decree two weeks ago imposing severe fines on state companies paying higher wages then regulated.
The average wage in the Bourgas shipyards was around 120,000 levs ($72) and the workers demanded wages to be increased to $120 per month, said Georgiev.
The Bourgas shipyards, one of the country's three shipbuilders, has 12,000 tonnes ouptput capacity, said Georgiev. At the moment it was repairing one ship.

The shipyard, due to be offered for privatisation this year, has posted 99 million levs profit for the first quarter of 1997 compared to a 32 million levs loss in the same period of the previous year, Georgiev said. ($=1.664 levs)
